messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/stream -> p99=4.6s (SLO=3.0s); p95=1.4s; source=tokenizer/preproc. Spike start=23:06 UTC.
Monique (on-call): Ack. Paging infra/runtime/ml. Notifying support & paging channel.
maya (support): Multiple reports from NimbusHealth integration; they describe streaming stalls and client-side timeouts. Collecting sample request ids: r_8a3f, r_8b10.
devops-bot: Runbook: https://runbook.internal/redwood/tokenizer-preproc-latency — follow step 1-4 for triage.
jared (infra): Observed sustained CPU and io-wait on pods tokenizer-preproc-{1..4}. Node pool tok-prep-np us-west-2a saturated. Queues backing up at ingress LB.
emma (ml): Looking at traces: expensive work located in preproc: JSON-mode schema validation + template rendering. Payloads with large tool schemas (~10-20kb) trigger deep-validate codepath. Example payload snippet: ```{"tool_schema": {"commands": [{"params": [{"name":"item","schema":{...}}]}}]}``` This causes recursive validation and allocations.
ryan (runtime): Reproduced locally with Nimbus payload. Root cause: new pretty-print step in prompt renderer (added to aid debugging) runs for JSON mode when message length > 2k; that pretty-print triggers validation in ml-preproc. Timing: pretty-print ~200-300ms, deep-validate ~1.2s on large schemas.
Monique (on-call): Immediate mitigations (ordered):
  1) Flip feature flag to disable JSON pretty-printing in prod (fast).
  2) Enable fast-json parser for payloads with tool_schema > 4kb.
  3) Scale tokenizer-preproc replicas by +5 in us-west-2 (temporary).
  4) Route NimbusHealth traffic to dedicated pool (route-id=r-nimbus-temp).
  5) Increase streaming client timeout at LB from 6s -> 12s for affected route.
devops-bot: Issuing flag change: /api/flags/set json-pretty-print=false (rollout-id r-19876).
ops-bot: scale: deployment/tokenizer-preproc +5 replicas in us-west-2 — started.
jared (infra): Scale in progress -> new pods coming up, pre-warming cache. Also evicting a noisy pod hogging disk I/O.
emma (ml): Pushed canary patch enabling `fast-json` (no deep-validate) for large schemas; canary on 2 pods now. Also added memoization of compiled templates (skips recompile if template hash matches).
ryan (runtime): Rolled back pretty-print change in 2026.02.14 release on canary; PR https://git.internal/r/9876. Streaming stalls decreased on canary.
Monique (on-call): Handoff planned at 23:30 UTC to emma. Monitoring for 30m. Please post p95/p99 numbers every 5m.
maya (support): Sent initial customer note to NimbusHealth: "We observed intermittent streaming stalls — mitigation steps applied (routing + parser fallback). We'll follow up with timeline and postmortem."
jared (infra): Initial synthetic test after mitigations: p99 reduced from 4.6s -> 2.4s, p95 ~1.2s. Live traffic shows slow but steady recovery.
emma (ml): Remaining: some older client libraries don't handle chunked streaming well which leads to perceived stalls. Plan: add chunked-flush every 100ms in runtime to ensure progress events. Patching runtime now to canary.
ryan (runtime): Canary runtime patch applied: `stream.flush_interval_ms=100` on 3 canaries. Early telemetry: number of stalled streams down 75%.
Monique (on-call): Good progress. Action items captured:
  - emma: finish fast-json rollout and template memoization; measure allocations.
  - jared: monitor node-level IO and autoscale policy; consider permanent replica increase for us-west tokenizers.
  - ryan: promote streaming flush patch to prod once canary stable.
  - maya: coordinate customer follow-up + ETA.
Monique (on-call): Handoff now to emma (23:30 UTC). I'll be reachable but stepping out for incident call.
emma (ml): Taking over. Filed incident ticket INC-19876. Starting 48h remediation plan: refactor deep-validate to iterative validator, add KV cache for tool_schema hashes, and add prompt-engine compiled-template cache. ETA preliminary fix 48-72h.
maya (support): NimbusHealth response: "Thanks for fast action. We're still seeing sporadic delays; will accept temporary timeout bump while you push fixes."
jared (infra): Observability note: capturing heap/alloc profiles for tokenizer-preproc pods for postmortem. Link: https://metrics.internal/redwood/heap/19876
Monique (on-call): Closing paging loop. Incident state -> monitoring. If regression, re-page immediately.
incident-bot: Incident INC-19876 state=monitoring severity=sev2
